summary: Tested the 5-model AI upgrade on the backend (12/12 pytest pass) and frontend (Playwright). Everything requested works: catalog, settings validation and saving, rule signal with models_used/macro_context, stats with model filter, progress endpoint, the engine=ai graceful failure (about 1.6s, 3 votes recorded as available:false), the drawer (toggles, last-model guard, presets, roles, cost hints, save, reload), run-cost-hint, macro-panel, the Deep AI progress-then-error flow, the Models column and the existing modals. Problems found: (1) every Deep AI or Council click sends 2 backend runs, which doubles LLM cost; (2) the ForexFactory calendar returns 429 and failed fetches are never cached, so macro data is always empty and the feed gets hit again on every request (51 x 429 in the log); (3) the win-rate tracker has no model filter in the UI.

critical.issue: ForexFactory returns 429 Too Many Requests (51 in backend.err.log). Failed fetches are not cached and there is no backoff or lock. Each signal request calls it 2+ times (_safe_macro plus _get_blackout_status) and concurrent requests all fetch. After a hot reload the in-memory cache is empty, so macro_context.events stays [] and the CPI/NFP/FOMC feature never shows data. The news blackout also silently stops working.

minor.issue: int(parsed.get('confidence')) at line ~1561 and int(bull.get('confidence_in_buy')) in council will raise a 500 if an LLM returns a non-numeric confidence (e.g. '75%'). Wrap in a safe parse.
A new rule signal is saved to ai_signals on every page load when the cache is missed. History shows many identical HOLD rows (same entry/SL/TP, seconds apart).
Can't verify the gold_bias/event_risk scoring with real events right now because the source returns 429. Only the empty-state structure was verified.

ui_bugs.issue: Deep AI/Council clicks send TWO /api/analysis/ai requests (confirmed in network: run_ids ...89184 and ...89198, 14ms apart). Cause: loadAI('ai') calls setEngine('ai'), which recreates the loadAI callback (engine is a dependency), and then useEffect([loadAI, refreshKey]) runs loadAI() a second time. This doubles LLM cost. Live progress polls the first runId while the result comes from whichever run finishes last.

After one Deep AI click, every timeframe change or toggle (auto-upgrade, blackout) re-runs the full paid multi-model engine automatically. If it fails, the rule signal and macro-panel disappear and only the ai-error shows. Consider falling back to the rule signal or going back to engine=rule on a timeframe change. Older requests are also not cancelled, so a stale response can overwrite a newer one.

integration_issues.issue: The backend supports /api/signals/stats?model= and returns by_model, but WinRateTracker.jsx only calls /signals/stats with no filter and never shows by_model. The approved 'stats filter by model' feature is missing from the UI.

issues: The title 'MACRO CALENDAR · CPI / NFP / FED' runs into 'GOLD NEUTRAL · RISK LOW' with no gap in the narrow sidebar ('FEDGOLD NEUTRAL'). It needs wrapping or a gap.
The 'Keep at least one model switched on' toast covers the Cancel/Save footer buttons at the bottom-right.

action_items: Fix the duplicate AI run in Dashboard.jsx: don't let setEngine retrigger the effect. For example, use a ref for engine, drop engine from the loadAI deps for forced runs, or guard with an in-flight ref or AbortController.

Add a negative cache or backoff to _fetch_economic_calendar: on failure, cache the stale or empty result for about 10 minutes, add an asyncio.Lock to stop concurrent fetches, and save the last good calendar to Mongo so it survives reloads.
Add a model filter (by_model) to WinRateTracker using /api/signals/stats?model=<id>.
Parse LLM confidence values safely (strip '%' and use try/except) to avoid 500s.
Fix spacing in the macro-panel header. Optionally fall back to the rule signal when Deep AI fails.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2638 lines. Split it into routers (ai, calendar, signals, ea, telegram).
The three risk-role AIVote blocks (aggressive/neutral/conservative) are near-identical, about 30 lines. Extract a helper.
_PROGRESS is in-memory per process. It is fine for a single worker but breaks with multiple uvicorn workers.
When the result comes from cache (180s), the progress endpoint returns no items for the new run_id. That is acceptable, but the UI shows no votes.
AISettings.preset is not validated against PRESETS keys (any string is accepted).

success_rate.backend: 100% (12/12 pytest); macro data unverifiable because ForexFactory returns 429
success_rate.frontend: ~85% (all requested testids work; duplicate-run bug and missing stats model filter)

seed_data_creation: No seed data. Test runs added rule/AI signal rows to ai_signals through normal API use. ai_settings were reset to the balanced preset at the end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: pytest tests/test_ai_models_macro.py -n 0 (the tests change shared ai_settings and must run sequentially). The LLM key is inactive, so engine=ai/council fail fast with 'All selected AI models failed to respond' / 'Council debate failed'. ForexFactory was rate-limiting (429). The ai_settings document once changed between my runs to a budget-roles/3-model mix, probably from another concurrent actor; it is now reset to balanced. Writing files under /app/backend/tests triggers a backend hot reload, which wipes the in-memory caches.
rca of the issue: Duplicate Deep AI request: Dashboard.jsx line 57 setEngine(forceEngine) inside loadAI, together with useCallback deps [.., engine, ..] and useEffect(() => loadAI(), [loadAI, refreshKey]) at line 79, runs a second fetch with engine='ai'. Macro empty: the ForexFactory 429 path returns the stale cache or [] and never sets the cache, so the next call fetches again right away, which keeps the rate limit going.
